findings.documented: API key sent as ?api_key=... query parameter
findings.actual: API key must be sent in the X-API-Key request header; query param gets a 401
findings.how_found: fetch script got a 401 with an explicit error message naming the header
findings.impact: every request built exactly as documented fails

findings.documented: only the API key is required to read collection endpoints
findings.actual: also requires a valid bearer token from POST /auth/login, or returns 401
findings.how_found: 401 'missing bearer token' when only the API key header was sent
findings.impact: a frontend built strictly from the docs never loads listings

findings.how_found: printed the raw login response; `data.token` was undefined
findings.impact: code following the docs literally never authenticates

findings.actual: response includes a refresh_token and a refresh_url (/auth/refresh)
findings.impact: combined with the real 15-minute token lifetime, a refresh flow is actually necessary for any session over 15 minutes

findings.documented: token valid for 24 hours (expires_in: 86400), single login enough for a session
findings.impact: a frontend holding one token for 30+ minutes (as required) will start getting 401s unless it refreshes

findings.actual: `page` is silently ignored; every value returns the same first records. Real pagination is via `offset`
findings.how_found: compared first/last listing_id across page=1,2,3 (identical) vs offset=0,50,100 (different)
findings.impact: a client built strictly from the docs can never see past the first page

findings.actual: capped at 50 regardless of requested limit
findings.impact: more requests needed than the docs imply

findings.actual: both fields are absent (undefined) on every collection response; only `total` and `results` are present
findings.impact: none functionally once known, but response shape doesn't match the doc

findings.documented: `total` is the exact number of records matching your filters
findings.actual: paging past `total` still returns genuine unique records; the real retrievable count (3500) exceeds the claimed total (3338) by 162, with zero duplicate IDs
findings.how_found: paged to where results.length reached total, then kept paging and got new unique IDs until the server finally returned an empty page
findings.impact: any client that trusts `total` as the stopping condition silently misses real records at the tail

findings.documented: returns only active listings; inactive/expired/withdrawn are excluded server side, so anything returned is safe to show
findings.how_found: counted is_live values across the full pulled dataset
findings.impact: a frontend trusting the doc would display inactive/withdrawn listings to users as if live

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees, integer
findings.actual: values are non-integer, crore-scale figures (e.g. 98.9, 5.83) requiring x10,000,000 to reach real rupees, roughly consistent with actual listing prices under the same projects
findings.how_found: top price_max values were all small decimals; cross-checked against real listing prices tied to the same project_ids after scaling
findings.impact: using the raw field value as rupees understates every project's price by 7 orders of magnitude

findings.documented: price_min and price_max describe a project's minimum and maximum unit price
findings.actual: for some projects, price_min is greater than price_max (values appear swapped/corrupted)
findings.how_found: compared price_min and price_max directly while sampling the largest projects by listing count
findings.impact: any code assuming min <= max will compute a negative or nonsensical range for these projects

findings.documented: listing objects describe real, physically coherent properties
findings.actual: a small number of records are physically impossible: negative/zero price, carpet_area exceeding super_built_up_area, floor exceeding total_floors, coordinates outside India, or a non-plot property with 0 bedrooms
findings.how_found: rule-based scan for logically impossible field combinations, cross-checked property_type to rule out legitimate 0-bedroom plots
findings.impact: these records cannot represent any real property and would mislead a buyer if shown as-is

findings.documented: listing objects represent real properties for sale
findings.actual: a subset of listings are priced at 30-40% of the median price/sqft for their locality+bedroom peer group with no other explanation (not corrupt data, not a locality/bedroom mismatch) — consistent with bait listings meant to generate enquiries rather than sell real inventory
findings.how_found: computed price/sqft per listing, grouped by locality+bedroom, flagged outliers below 40% of peer group median, after excluding already-corrupt (near-zero price) records
findings.impact: a user contacting these listings is likely enquiring about inventory that isn't genuinely available at the advertised price

findings.documented: total_listings is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with GET /v1/listings?project_id=...
findings.actual: 106 of 400 projects have a total_listings value that disagrees with the count of active (is_live=true) listings actually tied to that project_id
findings.how_found: counted active listings per project_id from the full pulled dataset and compared to each project's total_listings field
findings.impact: a dashboard trusting total_listings would show wrong inventory counts for over a quarter of projects
